correctness.rationale: Every allowed rim bit depends only on consecutive spoke directions; the signed two-state transfer counts them and subtracts the four forbidden global cycles. The reversal pairing and mod-four congruence prove exact even-rim support; explicit signed matrix products give multiplier −2; odd rim length gives 2^(n−1) additional even-weight zeros via off-diagonal products. Two independent exact integer implementations separately enumerate orientations and multiply transfer matrices, verifying all claimed finite checks through n=8. No extrapolation from code replaces the all-length proof.

value.rationale: For the natural family of wheel acyclic-orientation sets, the theorem gives exact signed Fourier multipliers in a linear number of integer transfer steps per frequency, identifies a sharp alternating parity transition in recoverable convolution modes, and quantifies the best-conditioned inverse on even wheels. The odd-wheel witness is a genuine non-symmetry information-loss mechanism, not a restatement of the known orientation count. This resolves a natural harmonic recovery question across all even sizes and gives infinite-family obstructions on odd sizes.
